hypotheses.justification: This follows from D. Each D.c k is a closed immersion, hence locally of finite type; awayι₀ is an open immersion, and ProjSpace.π is proper, hence locally of finite type. Composition and D.hover therefore give LocallyOfFiniteType ((D.U k).ι ≫ f). Apply IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_iSup_eq_top with D.hcov, install the resulting instance, and use the original proof. This argument also handles an empty indexing type.

Each D.U k is compact: D.c k is a closed embedding into an affine spectrum, so Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.compactSpace applies. D.hcov expresses X as a finite union of these compact opens, proving CompactSpace X. Since the target spectrum is quasi-separated, quasiCompact_of_compactSpace supplies QuasiCompact f, after which the original proof applies. The finite-union argument includes the empty-cover case.

The needed auxiliary results can be reproved without noetherianity by replacing its compactness argument. The remaining QuasiCompact f gives CompactSpace X. Each D.U k is compact by its closed embedding D.c k; X is quasi-separated because f is separated over an affine scheme. Finite intersections are compact by IsCompact.inter_of_isOpen, so D.Uo is compact (the empty intersection is X). D.XP is quasi-separated, hence quasiCompact_of_compactSpace gives QuasiCompact D.ψ. This replaces the noetherian-space instance used in the auxiliary proofs; their image, reducedness, irreducibility, and immersion arguments then proceed unchanged, yielding the displayed proof.

Replace the reducedness and irreducibility arguments by schematic density. The remaining noetherian and finite-type assumptions still make D.ψ quasi-compact. Scheme.Hom.toImage_app_injective shows that D.ψ' is schematically dense, also after restriction to D.V k. Thus ak_eq_bk follows without reducedness: its closed equalizer contains this schematically dense restriction, so its defining ideal is zero. The subsequent closed-immersion and properness arguments for ek still apply. Finally, its range is closed in D.O k and contains the dense range of D.ψ', so it is all of D.O k; neither irreducibility nor nonemptiness is needed. If D.Uo is empty, dominance of D.ψ' forces D.X' to be empty, and the equality holds too.
